renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: completeness_vs_duplication
  title: Completeness against duplication
  description: |-
    Each point is an assessed assembly, with the percent of complete BUSCOs on the horizontal axis and the percent of duplicated BUSCOs on the vertical axis, sized by contig N50 and coloured by lineage dataset. It answers which assemblies are both complete and free of duplication.
    How to read: the best assemblies sit far right and low. Points high on the vertical axis hold the same marker genes twice, which BUSCO explains by a recent genome duplication or by a chimeric assembly of haplotypes. A larger point is a more contiguous assembly.
    Note: BUSCO publishes no pass mark and asks that results be read in the biology of the organism, so no reference line is drawn.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Complete BUSCOs (%)
    y_title: Duplicated BUSCOs (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: complete_pct
    y: duplicated_pct
    label: assembly_id
    color: lineage
    size: contig_n50

- component: figure
  title: Complete BUSCOs per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assessed assembly, with the percent of its BUSCO markers found complete, coloured by the lineage dataset used. It answers which assemblies recover the most expected genes.
    How to read: a taller bar is a more complete assembly. Assemblies are only comparable when scored against the same lineage dataset, which the colour shows.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median percent of complete BUSCOs of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of BUSCO. BUSCO publishes no completeness cut-off.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembly_id
    y: complete_pct
    color: lineage
    labels:
      assembly_id: Assembly
      complete_pct: Complete BUSCOs (%)
      lineage: Lineage dataset
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: complete_pct

- component: card
  title: Complete BUSCOs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of complete BUSCOs over the assessed assemblies, and the box shows the spread. It answers how complete the assemblies are overall.
    How to read: a high median with a narrow box means a consistent set. A long lower whisker is an assembly that lost marker genes and deserves a look.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  column: complete_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Duplicated BUSCOs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of BUSCOs found more than once, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much redundancy the assemblies carry.
    How to read: BUSCO explains a high duplication by a recent genome duplication or by a chimeric assembly of haplotypes, and an unfiltered transcriptome or protein set also inflates it. Check the ploidy and the isoform handling of the input.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  column: duplicated_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Missing BUSCOs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of BUSCOs not found, and the box shows the spread. It answers how many expected genes the assemblies lack.
    How to read: BUSCO notes that missing genes may be of biological or technical origin. A tissue limited transcriptome is not expected to be BUSCO complete, so compare consistency across samples there.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  column: missing_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Assemblies assessed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct assemblies scored, and the strip gives the count of BUSCO runs. It answers how many assemblies the other tiles summarise.
    How to read: runs exceed assemblies when one assembly is scored in more than one mode, for example as a genome and as its annotated proteins.
  column: assembly_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: BUSCO runs behind it

- component: table
  title: BUSCO completeness per assembly
  description: |-
    Each row is a BUSCO run, with its lineage dataset, the complete, single-copy, duplicated, fragmented and missing percentages, the number of markers and the contiguity BUSCO measures. It answers the exact scores behind every other tile.
    How to read: sort by complete or by duplicated to rank assemblies, and read the lineage and mode columns before comparing two rows.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: class_composition
  title: BUSCO classes per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly, split into the four BUSCO classes that add up to the lineage set: complete single-copy, complete duplicated, fragmented and missing. It answers whether the genes an assembly lacks are lost or kept twice.
    How to read: a bar that is mostly complete single-copy is the target. A large duplicated part points at haplotypes or a duplication event, a large fragmented part at breaks inside gene models, and a large missing part at absent genes.
    Note: BUSCO publishes no cut-off for any class and asks for results to be read in the biology of the organism, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Share of BUSCO markers (%)
    x_title: Assembly
  roles:
    sample_id: assembly_id
    taxon: busco_class
    rank: rank
    abundance: percent

- component: advanced_viz
  id: class_composition_by_run
  title: BUSCO classes per run
  description: |-
    Each bar is one BUSCO run, split into the four BUSCO classes. An assembly scored in two modes, for example as a genome and as its annotated proteins, draws two bars. It answers how the same assembly compares between modes.
    How to read: a protein run that scores below its genome run points at an annotation that missed genes the assembly holds. Matching bars mean the annotation recovers what the assembly contains.
    Note: BUSCO publishes no cut-off for any class, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Share of BUSCO markers (%)
    x_title: BUSCO run
  roles:
    sample_id: run_id
    taxon: busco_class
    rank: rank
    abundance: percent

- component: figure
  title: BUSCO classes per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly, stacked by BUSCO class. It answers how the lineage set divides between complete single-copy, complete duplicated, fragmented and missing genes.
    How to read: the stack should add up to 100 percent, mostly complete single-copy. A stack split between two assessed modes of one assembly can exceed 100 percent, which the per-run tile above avoids.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembly_id
    y: percent
    color: busco_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      assembly_id: Assembly
      percent: Share of BUSCO markers (%)
      busco_class: BUSCO class

- component: card
  title: Complete single-copy BUSCOs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of BUSCO markers found complete and in one copy, and the box shows the spread over runs. It answers how many of the expected genes each assembly holds cleanly.
    How to read: this is the class to maximise. A box well below the others marks assemblies where genes are lost, fragmented or duplicated.
    Source: https://busco.ezlab.org/busco_userguide.html
  column: percent
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('busco_class') == 'Complete single-copy'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: BUSCO class composition
  description: |-
    Each row is one BUSCO class of one run, with its share of the lineage set in percent. It answers the exact share behind every bar.
    How to read: filter by class to compare one class across assemblies.
